entry.note: PDF verified: 'Giant Vortex Clusters in a Two-Dimensional Quantum Fluid' by Gauthier et al., arXiv:1801.06951. Vortex clusters in 2D BEC — matches QOU's vortex-condensation citation.

relevance.rationale: FILE ABSENT: the ledger row points at this path but the file does not exist anywhere in the working tree (verified by find over the whole repo; uploads/ holds 294 files and this is not one of them). The prior 2026-05-19 verification row therefore cannot be re-checked, and I could not confirm the seeded join against the document's own front matter. The verdict is undetermined on that ground alone. The corpus-side citation audit below did not need the document and is reported in full. CITATION AUDIT: one substantive site, observations/bec-vortex-data.md:13 (prose \cite) with the matching cites[] entry at bec-vortex-data.ts:12. The cited claim is specific and empirical: the block asserts that giant vortex clusters were observed in 2D 87-Rb condensates with same-sign vortices aggregating into macroscopic circulation structures, that 'the cluster circulation is quantised in multiples of the single-vortex quantum', and that this 'directly demonstrates the additive structure j_cluster = j_1 + j_2 + ...'. The registered entry's subject matches the first sentence closely enough that the attribution is plausible; what I cannot check without the document is the stronger second sentence - specifically whether the source reports quantisation of the CLUSTER circulation in units of the single-vortex quantum, as opposed to reporting clustering of individually-quantised same-sign vortices. The block then reads that additivity as SU_q(2) Clebsch-Gordan, which is the folio's own interpretive step and is correctly not attributed to the source.

proposedActions.rationale: The block leans on a specific empirical claim (cluster circulation quantised in multiples of the single-vortex quantum) that is stronger than the paper's title-level result and cannot be checked with the document missing. Either re-obtain it and add a figure/section locator, or weaken the sentence to what is uncontroversially reported.
